checks: No eclipse at 1 of 18 covered epochs where the 0.98593 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 216935767 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 3.00 percent and an orbital period of 0.9859 days, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 281.9 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 27.3, though a centroid offset of 1.4 arcsec was measured. No secondary eclipse was detected in the data. The candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a potentially new object. The pipeline's machine learning model assigned this target a screening score of 0.30, and the light curve passed all automated data quality checks.
